description: Human-curated strategy annotations for selected, famous ProofWiki results already present in the seed collection. Labels describe the displayed source proof, rather than asserting that these are the only proof methods for the result.

proofwiki:99e22b778d2ae35a4a0a46fd461df9.title: Pythagoras's Theorem
proofwiki:99e22b778d2ae35a4a0a46fd461df9.overview: A single theorem seen through dissection, Euclidean area, similar triangles, trigonometry, and cyclic geometry.
proofwiki:99e22b778d2ae35a4a0a46fd461df9.historical_note: The theorem is traditionally associated with ancient Greek mathematics; these are modern ProofWiki presentations, not transcriptions of historical sources.

proofwiki:proofwiki-19.label: Trigonometric identity
proofwiki:proofwiki-19.description: Derives the result from the sine-cosine identity and the right-triangle definitions of sine and cosine.

proofwiki:proofwiki-20.label: Euclidean area dissection
proofwiki:proofwiki-20.description: Uses the classical construction of squares on the three sides and compares congruent triangles with parallelograms.

proofwiki:proofwiki-21.label: Four-triangle area rearrangement
proofwiki:proofwiki-21.description: Computes the area of one large square in two ways after arranging four copies of the triangle.

proofwiki:proofwiki-22.label: Similar triangles
proofwiki:proofwiki-22.description: Uses the altitude to the hypotenuse and proportional sides in the resulting similar triangles.

proofwiki:proofwiki-23.label: Complementary-square area
proofwiki:proofwiki-23.description: Equates the area of a square with four triangles and a central complementary square.

proofwiki:proofwiki-24.label: Dissection and rearrangement
proofwiki:proofwiki-24.description: Cuts the square on the hypotenuse and rearranges the pieces into the two squares on the legs.

proofwiki:proofwiki-25.label: Equal-area square rearrangement
proofwiki:proofwiki-25.description: Compares two decompositions of equal large squares after cancelling four congruent triangles.

proofwiki:proofwiki-27.label: Similarity and area ratios
proofwiki:proofwiki-27.description: Uses the altitude construction, similarity, and ratios of areas to recover the side-square identity.

proofwiki:proofwiki-28.label: Cyclic quadrilateral and Ptolemy
proofwiki:proofwiki-28.description: Places a rectangle on a circumcircle and applies Ptolemy's theorem.

proofwiki:proofwiki-29.label: Similarity with altitudes
proofwiki:proofwiki-29.description: Combines similarity ratios with an area decomposition of the original triangle.

proofwiki:1da31213790cf42b6bae98efcab61d.title: Square Root of 2 is Irrational
proofwiki:1da31213790cf42b6bae98efcab61d.overview: The familiar statement has parity, descent, polynomial, and analytic-style routes.
proofwiki:1da31213790cf42b6bae98efcab61d.historical_note: The result is traditionally linked to early Greek mathematics; the proofs here are modern ProofWiki presentations.

proofwiki:proofwiki-143.label: Parity contradiction
proofwiki:proofwiki-143.description: A lowest-terms fraction would force both numerator and denominator to be even.

proofwiki:proofwiki-144.label: Prime-root theorem
proofwiki:proofwiki-144.description: Reduces the claim to the general theorem that the square root of a prime is irrational.

proofwiki:proofwiki-145.label: Integer bound from binomial expansion
proofwiki:proofwiki-145.description: Builds integer expressions from powers of √2−1 and derives a contradiction from their size.

proofwiki:proofwiki-146.label: Infinite descent
proofwiki:proofwiki-146.description: Transforms a supposed representation into one with a strictly smaller positive denominator.

proofwiki:proofwiki-147.label: Rational root theorem
proofwiki:proofwiki-147.description: Rules out every possible rational root of x²−2.

proofwiki:7c867f57f0efc7d0ec5271daedeca4.title: Fermat's Little Theorem
proofwiki:7c867f57f0efc7d0ec5271daedeca4.overview: The result is approached through residue permutations, finite groups, binomial coefficients, and cyclic actions.

proofwiki:proofwiki-91.label: Necklace counting
proofwiki:proofwiki-91.description: Counts p-bead colorings by rotation orbits to obtain the equivalent congruence nᵖ ≡ n mod p.

proofwiki:proofwiki-92.label: Permutation of nonzero residues
proofwiki:proofwiki-92.description: Multiplication by n permutes the nonzero residue classes modulo p.

proofwiki:proofwiki-93.label: Euler totient specialization
proofwiki:proofwiki-93.description: Obtains the theorem as the prime-modulus case of Euler's theorem.

proofwiki:proofwiki-94.label: Finite-group order
proofwiki:proofwiki-94.description: Applies the order of the multiplicative group of nonzero residues modulo p.

proofwiki:proofwiki-95.label: Binomial induction
proofwiki:proofwiki-95.description: Uses the divisibility of intermediate binomial coefficients by p in an induction argument.

proofwiki:proofwiki-96.label: Burnside orbit count
proofwiki:proofwiki-96.description: Counts fixed p-tuples under cyclic shifts using Burnside's lemma.

proofwiki:f30b71a53b6c44b7488b08861f9dfe.title: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
proofwiki:f30b71a53b6c44b7488b08861f9dfe.overview: A foundational existence theorem with topological, complex-analytic, algebraic, and minimization arguments.

proofwiki:proofwiki-1597.label: Homotopy and winding
proofwiki:proofwiki-1597.description: Deforms the polynomial to its leading monomial and uses topological behavior on a large circle.

proofwiki:proofwiki-1598.label: Liouville's theorem
proofwiki:proofwiki-1598.description: A zero-free polynomial would give a bounded entire reciprocal, hence a contradiction.

proofwiki:proofwiki-1599.label: Contour integral
proofwiki:proofwiki-1599.description: Uses a contour integral estimate and holomorphicity under the assumption of no root.

proofwiki:proofwiki-1600.label: Algebraic induction on degree
proofwiki:proofwiki-1600.description: Reduces degrees through an induction argument using real polynomials and splitting fields.

proofwiki:proofwiki-1601.label: Minimum-modulus argument
proofwiki:proofwiki-1601.description: Uses growth at infinity to find a minimum of |p| and shows a positive minimum is impossible.

proofwiki:proofwiki-1602.label: Cauchy integral formula
proofwiki:proofwiki-1602.description: Combines Cauchy's integral formula with a large-circle estimate for the reciprocal.

proofwiki:26679abbccff819bb46e38a67d186b.title: Unique Prime Factorization
proofwiki:26679abbccff819bb46e38a67d186b.overview: Three compact arguments show how minimality, cancellation, and induction enforce uniqueness.

proofwiki:proofwiki-5522.label: Minimal counterexample
proofwiki:proofwiki-5522.description: Assumes a least integer with two prime factorizations and constructs a smaller counterexample.

proofwiki:proofwiki-5523.label: Euclid's lemma and cancellation
proofwiki:proofwiki-5523.description: Matches a prime factor across two products, cancels it, and repeats.

proofwiki:proofwiki-5524.label: Strong induction
proofwiki:proofwiki-5524.description: Proves uniqueness for each integer from the uniqueness of smaller prime decompositions.
